title: Orb of Sacrifice Family Guide
summary: The four Orbs of Sacrifice from Atziri's Vault upgrade a corruption enchantment on matching rare equipment and remove one random explicit modifier. This guide answers whether each orb can be used, what it is worth, and what to check first.
description: A source-linked reference for the Orb of Sacrifice family: four orbs, valid targets, risks, before-and-after outcomes, and decision guidance.
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial Team
imageAlt: Yaomac's Orb of Sacrifice currency item icon - a fiery corruption orb from Atziri's Vault

sections.title: Quick answer: can you use it, is it worth it
sections.callout: Use an Orb of Sacrifice only when the target is an already-corrupted rare item that owns a corruption enchantment you want upgraded, and you can accept losing any single explicit modifier.
calloutDetail: The four orbs are not interchangeable: each is bound to a category of equipment.
Every use permanently removes one random explicit modifier, so the decision is never just 'an upgrade'.

answers.label: Sell first
text: Sell the orb if you do not understand the enchantment upgrade pool, or if the orb is worth more than the item you would target.

answers.label: Hold first
text: Hold it if the gear is still transitional, or if losing any modifier would break the build, because there is no backup once applied.

answers.label: Use it
text: Use it when the target, risk, and replacement are all planned, and you accept the worst-case modifier loss.

sections.title: The four orbs map to four equipment categories
intro: All four orbs share one rule: upgrade the corruption enchantment on a matching corrupted rare item, then remove one random explicit modifier. The difference is only which equipment they accept.

members.title: Yaomac's Orb of Sacrifice
body: Targets rare weapons or quivers that are already corrupted and own a corruption enchantment.

members.title: Kopec's Orb of Sacrifice
body: Targets rare helmets, chestplates, gloves, and boots that are already corrupted and own a corruption enchantment.

members.title: Kamasa's Orb of Sacrifice
body: Targets rare amulets, rings, and belts that are already corrupted and own a corruption enchantment.

members.title: Yugul's Orb of Sacrifice
body: Targets rare jewels that are already corrupted and own a corruption enchantment.

sections.title: Valid target matrix
note: A target must be rare, corrupted, of the matching item class, and already own a corruption enchantment. Missing any condition makes the orb unusable.

rows.label: Rare weapon / quiver
rows.note: Must already own a corruption enchantment.

rows.label: Rare armour
rows.note: Confirm the piece is in the armour class.

rows.label: Rare amulet / ring / belt
rows.note: Jewellery core modifiers are often the hardest to lose.

rows.label: Rare jewel
rows.note: Confirm the jewel enchantment can be upgraded.

sections.title: How to get them
intro: These orbs are not a normal world drop. They come from the end of the Vaal Temple chain, behind Atziri's Vault.

routes.label: Build and progress the Vaal Temple
body: Complete the Temple route and unlock the path that leads to Atziri.

routes.label: Defeat Atziri, the Red Queen
body: The Orbs of Sacrifice drop from the vault opened after defeating Atziri.

routes.label: Check which of the four dropped
body: The vault can drop any one of the four; a single kill does not guarantee a specific orb.

routes.label: Trade or use
body: Market prices must use timestamped data; never write a fixed 'always' price into static text.

items.label: Item class matches the orb
checks: Confirm the orb name maps to the target's item class using the matrix above.
items.why: Wrong pairing means the orb cannot be applied at all.
items.fix: Switch to the correct orb for this equipment category.

items.label: Already a corrupted rare item
checks: Check the tooltip for both the Rare and Corrupted labels.
items.why: Missing either label fails the target condition.
items.fix: Only apply to items that already meet both states.

items.label: Owns an upgradable corruption enchantment
checks: Confirm the enchantment exists and what it can roll into using a database reference.
items.why: Without it there is no defined benefit target.
items.fix: Research the upgrade pool before committing.

items.label: List every explicit modifier
checks: Mark each modifier as 'can lose' or 'cannot lose'.
items.why: Losing a build-core modifier bricks the item.
items.fix: Do not use if any modifier is non-negotiable.

items.label: Prepare a replacement item
checks: Place a backup in inventory or stash.
items.why: Failure leaves the build unable to function.
items.fix: Only proceed with a real fallback ready.

items.label: Compare orb and item market value
checks: Use a dated market snapshot, not feeling.
items.why: Spending a high-value orb on a low-value base wastes currency.
items.fix: Sell the orb if it is worth more than the target.

steps.label: Right-click the orb
body: The client enters the apply-currency state.

steps.label: Select a valid target
body: Confirm class, rarity, corruption, and enchantment.

steps.label: Confirm the risk
body: One explicit modifier is removed at random.

steps.label: Review the result
body: Record the upgraded enchantment and the removed modifier.

before: Four explicit modifiers, one of which will be removed at random.
after: Enchantment upgraded, one explicit modifier gone, item now permanently changed.

sections.title: Use, sell, or hold
marketNote: Price blocks may only show region, league, timestamp, and source. Static text must never promise a fixed exchange rate.

use.first: Confirm the item will not fail if any single modifier is lost
use.condition: You have a replacement and the enchantment upgrade is clearly valuable
use.risk: A random core modifier is removed
text: Before using, build the 'can-lose' list. If any modifier is non-negotiable, describe the use as an ordinary upgrade.

sell.first: Check the orb price against the target item price
sell.condition: The orb is worth more than the item, or you do not understand the upgrade pool
sell.risk: You lose a high-value orb on a low-value base
text: Sell when the currency value exceeds the expected benefit of the upgrade.

hold.first: Confirm the gear is not still transitional
hold.condition: You lack a replacement or the build still depends on every modifier
hold.risk: Using now could brick the only working piece
text: Hold until the build is stable and a backup exists.

intro: These orbs matter most for builds that depend on a specific corruption enchantment. List the modifiers you absolutely cannot lose before considering use.

entries.question: My upgraded resistance enchantment is strong, but I also lost an ordinary modifier.
summary: A player showed a corrupted enchantment upgraded after using an Orb of Sacrifice and discussed whether the high resistance was worth the lost modifier.
editorialAnalysis: The case proves the upside can be high, but a single success does not represent the average result. Pages must show both the success and the failure cost.
officialAnswer: Decide using the worst-case removed modifier, not the best upgraded result.

entries.question: Can I use Yaomac's orb to push my staff's skill level higher?
summary: A player hoped to raise skill level by upgrading a weapon corruption enchantment, while worrying about losing cast speed or a normal skill-level modifier.
editorialAnalysis: This must be judged together with the build page, not only by the enchantment ceiling.
officialAnswer: List the受益 builds and the non-negotiable modifiers directly below the article.

entries.question: Why does my orb not apply at all?
summary: Common causes are mismatched item class, not rare, no corruption enchantment, or the wrong one of the four orbs.
editorialAnalysis: Most 'cannot use' reports are target-condition mistakes, not client bugs.
officialAnswer: Check the compatibility matrix item by item before clicking again.

problems.symptom: The client says this item cannot use the Orb of Sacrifice
directAnswer: The most common cause is orb-to-equipment mismatch, or the target is not a corrupted rare item that owns a corruption enchantment.
checks: Confirm the orb name and the target class.
Confirm the Rare and Corrupted labels.
Confirm a corruption enchantment exists on the tooltip.

problems.symptom: Can one item be used multiple times?
directAnswer: Whether repeated use is possible depends on the remaining enchantment state and the current client rules; confirm with the current version, not a community single case.
checks: Check the current client behaviour before assuming repeated use.

problems.symptom: How is this different from Architect's Orb?
directAnswer: Orb of Sacrifice upgrades a corruption enchantment on matching rare items and sacrifices a random explicit modifier; Architect's Orb is a different high-risk currency for corrupted items.
checks: Read the Architect's Orb article for the separate risk profile.

items.question: Can I use these on Uniques?
answer: No. The valid targets are rare, corrupted items of the matching class that already own a corruption enchantment.

items.question: Does the market price stay fixed?
answer: No. Any price shown must be timestamped with region and league; static text never promises a fixed rate.

items.question: Should I use it on league-start gear?
answer: Usually no. League-start characters rarely have a spare to absorb a failed roll.
